```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(depprep)
```

Satellite images, monitoring stations or repeated surveys give every variable at every
site and time. The large-scale structure can then be a common time series, a map with a
seasonal amplitude, or a pattern that moves (a plume, a front). `depprep` needs a
complete grid: every site at every time.

## Data with known truth

```{r simulate}
g <- sim_groups(sim_group("common", 3, "temporal_common", phi = 0.9),
                sim_group("seasonal_map", 3, "separable_seasonal", range = 0.25, period = 12),
                sim_group("moving", 3, "moving", range = 0.25, velocity = c(0.02, 0)),
                sim_group("none", 2, "none"))
sim <- sim_spatiotemporal(50, 60, g, seed = 3)
dim(sim$X)               # 50 sites x 60 times, 11 variables
head(sim$index)
```

With your own data, give the site coordinates (`coords`, one row per site) and an
`index` with the `site` (row of `coords`) and `time` of every observation.

## Diagnose, group, correct

```{r workflow}
sig <- diagnose_variables(sim, nsim = 99)
gr <- group_regimes(sig)
gr[, c("variable", "type", "group")]
cr <- correct(sim, gr)
cr$mode
```

On a grid this small the diagnosis can read the seasonal maps and the moving pattern as
a common series (each regime needs enough sites and times to be told apart); check the
table, and change a regime by hand in `run_app()` when you know better.

In space-time the default for the correlation matrix is whitening group by group: the
common processes persist in time and the residuals do not, so filtering by the temporal
model separates them better than a basis. The data matrix keeps one basis per variable.

## Verify

```{r verify}
v <- verify(cr, sim, nperm = 0)
v$delta_summary
```

The spatial tests and the local Moran's I are computed on the site means of the
corrected variables.

## A moving pattern

For a pattern that moves in a known direction (here along x), directional maps can be
offered to the group's spatial margin, together with the temporal maps:

```{r menu}
m <- basis_menu(term_trend(), term_aem(direction = 0), term_mem(margin = "time"))
b <- build_group_basis(sim$X[, sim$group == "moving"], coords = sim$coords, index = sim$index, menu = m)
attr(b, "k")
head(attr(b, "terms"))
```
